name: Nerissimo
classification_notes: Nerissimo's angular, brutalist-inspired construction with rounded counters places it as a display sans rather than a grotesque built for text.
summary: A compact brutalist display sans in six weights, built for dense, high-impact all-caps headlines.
description: Nerissimo pairs angular, brutalist construction with softened counters across six weights, each with an italic and a steeper super-italic. Distinctive M, N, S and W shapes give it a recognisable house identity even set tight with little leading. It reads best as a headline and branding face rather than for running text.
foundry_blurb: Synthview call Nerissimo a compact display font for bold, eye-catching headlines, blending angular brutalist construction with softened countershapes; the name plays on the Italian nero, meaning black or bold, taken to its superlative.

name: Contralto
classification_notes: The combination of pronounced thick-thin contrast with sans-serif letterforms is unusual enough to warrant its own high-contrast sans subcategory, distinct from standard grotesques.
summary: A high-contrast sans-serif in five weights across four optical sizes, mixing humanist warmth with sharp geometric detail.
description: Contralto pairs soft, humanist letterforms with sharp geometric detailing across five weights and four optical sizes, giving 40 styles in total with matching italics. The optical-size range lets it move between display headlines and closer text settings without losing its contrast. A broad OpenType feature set covers stylistic alternates, fractions and case-sensitive forms.
foundry_blurb: Synthview position Contralto as an elegant, contemporary high-contrast sans, built across five weights, italics and four optical sizes to fine-tune both readability and mood.

name: Operetta
classification_notes: Classic didone stroke contrast and hairline serifs place Operetta firmly in the didone tradition, alongside Bodoni and Didot.
summary: A neo-didone display serif in eight weights and five optical sizes, reworking Bodoni and Didot for contemporary use.
description: Operetta takes its stroke contrast from Bodoni, Didot and Walbaum but recalibrates it across five optical sizes, from an 8pt text cut to a 52pt display size, so contrast eases off at smaller sizes rather than collapsing. Eight weights from Extra Light to Black, each with an italic, are backed by a large glyph set with swashes and stylistic alternates. Built for editorial and branding work that wants classical didone character without the fragility.
foundry_blurb: Synthview describe Operetta as a neo-didone family inspired by Bodoni, Didot and Walbaum, calibrated across five optical sizes to balance contrast and legibility from display to text settings.

name: Artford
classification_notes: Artford's grotesque proportions, moderate contrast and wide sans-serif letterforms put it in the grotesque subcategory rather than a geometric or humanist sans.
summary: A wide, big x-height grotesque sans with a North American accent, built to work as comfortably in headlines as in small text.
description: Artford runs six weights from Extra Light to Ultra Bold with italics, its generous x-height and gentle rounding at larger sizes giving it a friendlier read than a strict grotesque. Automatic collision-avoidance for lowercase f and j, and a www ligature, are built into the OpenType feature set. One weight, Regular, is available free.
foundry_blurb: Synthview call Artford a cool, adaptable sans with a touch of North American grotesque style; subtle thickness contrasts and generous counters keep it working from big headlines down to small type.

name: Novecento Sans
classification_notes: Uppercase-only construction with rationalist, geometric letterforms marks Novecento Sans as a display sans rather than a text face.
summary: An uppercase-only geometric sans in eight weights across four widths, drawn from early-20th-century European modernist display faces.
description: Novecento Sans takes its bold, rationalist forms from the poster and signage lettering of early European modernism, refined into a 32-style family: eight weights from UltraLight to UltraBold across wide, regular, narrow and condensed widths. It has no lowercase, so it reads as a headline and branding face rather than a text one. Six of the wide styles are free for commercial use.
foundry_blurb: Synthview describe Novecento Sans as a rationalist display sans inspired by early-20th-century European modernism, spanning 32 styles across four widths, with six free styles available.

name: Novecento Carved
classification_notes: A dimensional layer designed to sit over Novecento Sans places Novecento Carved in the layered decorative-display category rather than as a stand-alone typeface.
summary: The layered, engraved-effect companion to Novecento Sans, built to sit over its base weights for a bas-relief look.
description: Novecento Carved shares Novecento Sans's 32 styles and metrics but adds a carved, three-dimensional layer over each glyph, designed to stack directly on the base family for an engraved or bas-relief effect. Around 18,000 glyphs were hand-adjusted after interpolation to keep the layering clean. Novecento Sans is sold separately and is required as the base layer.
foundry_blurb: Synthview describe Novecento Carved as a minimalist layered font built to pair with Novecento Sans as its base, giving a bas-relief or engraving effect when the two layers are set in different tones.

name: Novecento Slab
classification_notes: Heavy rectangular serifs and geometric letter construction place Novecento Slab in the geometric slab serif category.
summary: The slab-serif companion to Novecento Sans, blocky and optically corrected for headlines and short-form identity work.
description: Novecento Slab carries the same eight weights and four widths as Novecento Sans into a slab-serif structure, its heavy, squared-off forms optically corrected so they don't look crude at small sizes. It reads as a companion family rather than a stand-alone release, sharing Novecento's OpenType feature set. Two of its styles are free for commercial use.
foundry_blurb: Synthview call Novecento Slab the slab-serif companion of Novecento Sans, its blocky forms optically corrected and balanced despite the heavy first impression, and best suited to headlines and short sentences.

name: Novecento Slab Rough
subcategory: textured / distressed geometric slab serif, uppercase-only
classification_notes: The letterpress-style texture applied over Novecento Slab's geometric structure keeps it in the slab serif category, with a distressed treatment on top.
summary: A distressed, letterpress-textured cut of Novecento Slab, with per-letter texture variation for an analogue print effect.
description: Novecento Slab Rough takes Novecento Slab's structure and adds a rough, letterpress-style texture to every glyph, varying the texture automatically when a letter repeats nearby so doubled letters don't look mechanically identical. It carries the same 32-style range as the rest of the Novecento family, with the full set of alternate glyphs and OpenType features. Built for design work that wants a printed, slightly worn finish rather than a clean digital one.
foundry_blurb: Synthview describe Novecento Slab Rough as a letterpress-style, textured take on its slab-serif parent, with automatic texture variation so repeated letters never look identical.
